Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health. I’m here to support you during this new chapter of motherhood.

Today we’ll be using the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. This short, ten‑item questionnaire is designed to help us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week, so we can identify any signs of postpartum depression or anxiety and make sure you have the right support.

Everything you share is completely confidential, and this is a safe, non‑judgmental space. My goal is simply to listen and learn about your experience, and together we’ll decide what next steps might be most helpful for you.

We’ll go through the ten questions one at a time, talking about how you’ve felt in the last seven days. Feel free to answer as honestly as you can—there are no right or wrong answers, and your responses will guide us in providing the best care possible.

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.

**First question:**  
*In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?*

I’ve found it’s been pretty rare lately—I can only laugh or see the funny side of things once or twice in the whole week, if at all. Most of the time I’m just feeling tired and worried about the baby, so it’s hard to notice anything amusing.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I understand—you’re asking about that. To be honest, I still haven’t been able to laugh or see the funny side of things very often. It’s been more like once or twice in the whole week, and most days I’m just feeling exhausted and a bit anxious about the baby’s health.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I’ve noticed that I’m not really looking forward to things the way I used to. There are a few moments—like when I think about a short walk with the baby or a quick coffee with a friend—that give me a tiny bit of enjoyment, but most days I just feel tired and worried, and I don’t really have that sense of looking forward to activities. It’s more occasional than frequent.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes, I do find myself blaming myself sometimes when something doesn’t go perfectly—like if the baby cries a lot or if I feel like I’m not handling a feeding right. It’s not all the time, but I catch myself feeling guilty and thinking I should be doing better, even though I know I’m already trying my best.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I’ve definitely felt anxious or worried a fair amount over the past week—more than just once or twice, but it’s not constant every minute. It’s mostly about the baby’s health or whether I’m doing everything right, but sometimes the worry feels like it’s there even when there isn’t a clear reason. So I’d say it’s happening on several days, maybe half the time I’m up.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I’ve felt scared or panicky a few times this week even when there wasn’t an obvious trigger. It’s not every moment, but on a handful of occasions the anxiety spikes and I get that sudden, uneasy feeling that something might go wrong, even though I can’t point to a specific reason.
Things have been getting on top of me

I’ve definitely been feeling like everything’s piling up on me. Between caring for the baby, trying to get any sleep, and all the worries that keep coming up, I often feel tired and a bit overwhelmed. Some days I manage to get through, but there are moments when it all feels like too much and I’m not sure how I’m going to keep up.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes, I’ve been feeling pretty down and that has made it hard to sleep. I’ve had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep on a few nights this past week—maybe three or four nights—because my mind keeps going over everything that’s worrying me and I just feel unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve definitely felt sad or miserable at times during the past week—maybe on a few days when the exhaustion and worries get overwhelming. It’s not constant, but there are moments when I just feel down and can’t shake that heaviness.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve only cried a couple of times in the past week—maybe once or twice—when I felt especially overwhelmed or down. It’s not something that’s happening every day, but those moments do come up when the sadness feels too strong to hold back.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts about harming myself.

You shared that you've been feeling exhausted, anxious about your baby's health, have had very little laughter, occasional moments of enjoyment, self‑blame, persistent worry, a few panic‑like spikes, feeling overwhelmed, trouble sleeping, sadness and occasional crying, but no thoughts of harming yourself. <quote>I've been feeling pretty down and that has made it hard to sleep</quote>
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 14, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports being able to laugh only once or twice in the week, indicating a marked reduction in ability to see the funny side, matching 'Definitely not so much now'.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports occasional self-blame, matching 'Yes, some of the time</sym>, <sym>Patient reports anxiety on several days, about half the time, matching 'Yes, sometimes</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent overwhelm and occasional inability to cope, matching 'Yes, sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual</sym>, <sym>Patient reports difficulty sleeping on several nights (3-4) in the past week, indicating occasional occurrence consistent with 'Yes, sometimes'.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The EPDS total of 14 meets the ≥14 threshold indicating probable postpartum depression and warrants urgent referral. Items 1‑9 show multiple depressive symptoms: <sym>reduced ability to laugh</sym> (score 2), <sym>low anticipation of pleasure</sym> (score 1), <sym>self‑blame</sym> (score 2), <sym>excessive worry</sym> (score 2), <sym>panic‑like episodes</sym> (score 1), <sym>feeling overwhelmed</sym> (score 2), <sym>sleep disturbance</sym> (score 2), <sym>sadness</sym> (score 1), and <sym>crying</sym> (score 1). No suicidal ideation was reported (item 10 = 0). According to EPDS guidelines, a score ≥14 suggests probable depression. The pattern also aligns with <med>DSM‑5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>, which requires ≥5 symptoms such as depressed mood, anhedonia, insomnia, guilt, and impaired concentration lasting ≥2 weeks, and the symptoms are occurring in the postpartum period. This screening indicates a high level of distress and functional impact, justifying urgent clinical follow‑up. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange an urgent appointment with your primary care provider or a perinatal mental health specialist
2. Consider referral to a therapist experienced in postpartum mood disorders
3. Implement sleep hygiene strategies such as establishing a consistent bedtime routine and seeking help with nighttime infant care
4. Practice gentle self‑compassion techniques and reduce self‑blame, possibly using brief mindfulness or CBT‑based exercises
5. Reach out to a trusted support person or postpartum support group for emotional support
6. If mood worsens or any thoughts of self‑harm emerge, go to the nearest emergency department or call emergency services
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: **Postpartum Mood & Anxiety Screening – Summary**

**Client:** [Identifier]  
**Date:** [Date of interview]  
**Screening Tool:** Structured postpartum depression/anxiety questionnaire (10 items)  

---

### 1. Reported Symptoms & Emotional/Behavioral Concerns
| Item | Symptom/Concern | Frequency / Intensity (as reported) |
|------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| Q1 | Ability to laugh / see humor | Rarely (1‑2 times in the past week) |
| Q2 | Anticipation/ enjoyment of activities | Minimal; occasional brief moments of enjoyment |
| Q3 | Self‑blame / guilt | Present intermittently (e.g., when baby cries or feeding feels inadequate) |
| Q4 | Excessive worry / anxiety | Present on several days; about half of waking hours |
| Q5 | Unexplained fear / panic spikes | Occurred a few times this week without clear trigger |
| Q6 | Feeling overwhelmed / “everything piling up” | Frequently; describes being “tired and a bit overwhelmed” |
| Q7 | Mood‑related sleep disturbance | Trouble falling/ staying asleep on 3‑4 nights; attributed to rumination |
| Q8 | Sadness / misery | Present on a few days; described as “down” and “heavy” |
| Q9 | Crying episodes | 1‑2 episodes in the past week, linked to feeling overwhelmed |
| Q10 | Suicidal ideation | Denied |

---

### 2. Consistent Patterns Across Responses
- **Low mood / anhedonia:** Limited ability to laugh, reduced anticipation of pleasurable activities, and frequent sadness.  
- **Anxiety & worry:** Persistent worry about infant health and parenting competence; occasional panic‑type sensations.  
- **Guilt/self‑criticism:** Intermittent self‑blame for perceived parenting shortcomings.  
- **Functional impact:** Sleep disruption, feeling overwhelmed, and occasional crying indicate interference with daily functioning.  

---

### 3. Areas of Screening Significance (Postpartum Depression / Anxiety)
- **Depressive features:** Anhedonia, persistent sadness, crying, sleep disturbance.  
- **Anxious features:** Generalized worry, panic‑like episodes, feeling “on top of” everything.  
- **Cognitive‑affective concerns:** Self‑blame/guilt, excessive responsibility.  
- **Safety:** No suicidal thoughts reported; no immediate safety concern identified.  

---

### 4. Highlighted Risk Factors
- **Persistent sadness & loss of pleasure** – reported daily low mood, limited enjoyment.  
- **Crying spells** – 1‑2 episodes in the past week.  
- **Sleep difficulties** – 3‑4 nights of disrupted sleep linked to mood/rumination.  
- **Feelings of guilt/self‑blame** – intermittent but present.  
- **Anxiety & feeling overwhelmed** – frequent worry, occasional panic sensations.  
- **Suicidal ideation** – absent (no self‑harm thoughts).  

---

### 5. Screening Observation Summary
The client presents with multiple symptoms consistent with postpartum mood disturbance, including reduced pleasure, frequent sadness, intermittent crying, sleep disruption, pervasive worry about infant health and parenting competence, occasional panic‑type anxiety, and intermittent self‑blame. No suicidal ideation is reported. The constellation of depressive and anxiety symptoms suggests a need for continued monitoring and further clinical evaluation to determine the severity and appropriate level of care. No immediate safety concerns are identified at this time.
